newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Tyumen Oil Company sale seen Oct 1-Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: Russian Tyumen Oil Company sale seen Oct 1-Nov 20.

text.p: Russia will sell off part of the Tyumen Oil Company through a cash auction set for October 1-November 20, but the size of the stake and terms of the sale have not yet been set.

The Russian Federal Property Fund said in its latest Reforma bulletin on Monday that property officials had signed decrees fixing the dates during which bids would be accepted for the company, known as TNK.
The auction was originally to have been held August 5-September 26 but was postponed. Under the original scheme, a 48.64 percent stake was to be sold for cash.
Novy Holding, a Russian company backed by the Alfa Group financial-industrial concern, won a 40 percent stake in TNK for $810 million in an investment tender in July.

TNK, whose main crude oil production unit is Nizhnevartovskneftegaz, is one of the larger energy companies due to come on to the auction blocks. It produced 21.3 million tonnes (426,000 barrels per day) of crude last year.
Russia plans a number of sell-offs to help fill gaping holes in government coffers.
